Copilot vs local vs cloud

A harness is the environment that hosts an agent and gives it access to models, tools, and workspaces. These labels describe common setups; exact behavior depends on the VS Code host, provider, and organization policy.

Practical differences between the three harness choices
Harness Where it runs / access Best suited for Main consideration
Copilot Uses the Copilot-managed agent experience and the capabilities enabled by your VS Code setup and account. Interactive work in the editor; a convenient default when you want built-in integration. Available models, tools, and execution behavior are governed by the host and your organization’s settings.
Local Runs agent tools on your machine, with access to local files and processes granted to that runtime. Direct control over local development tools or workflows that need your local environment. Local execution does not necessarily mean local model inference; model requests may still use a remote provider.
Cloud Runs in a remote environment with repository and tool access provided by that service. Background or longer-running work that should not depend on your workstation staying active. Check what repository data is transferred, what permissions are granted, and any isolation or usage limits.

Quick recommendation

Privacy reminder: “Local” describes where agent tools run, not necessarily where the model processes prompts. Confirm model routing and data policies for your specific host before using sensitive code.
